fun_highlights: The callback system genuinely produces emergent arcs. cb_lookaway fires decades after c_friend's 'Look away' choice with a lived-in reference to exactly how many years have passed ('a debt 27 years overdue' in Hale Okonkwo's life, '42 years overdue' in Mira Halloran's). This is the engine's best emergence: the past literally names itself at the moment of reckoning. Similarly, cb_books_late closes the loop on c_book with the specific age the book was first picked up. These are the moments that make the genre feel earned rather than procedural.

The five-life Okonkwo dynasty (Dynasty 4) shows genuine systemic variety that the design earned: Calla the lifelong drifter, Elias the war-touched son born into her poverty, Noor the restless daughter who tries to pick a thing at 50 and fails, Beatrix the guarded achiever who silently breaks a promise at 40 and carries it, Hale the wanderer who finally honours the founder. Each generation reads different because the calling system, the collateral-succession mechanic, and the heirloom layer actually compound. The dynasty-layer is doing real work here.

Era-coloring of the calling card (y_calling) is a genuine systemic collision point. A war-era calling reads 'There is a war on, and it is hungry for the young' and nudges soldier choices; a hard-era calling reads 'In a lean time, the choice of what to be is also the choice of how to eat.' Across the 15 dynasties these land meaningfully differently: Elias Okonkwo's war-era call ('answered the call he could have dodged') feels shaped by his world in a way that Cassian Thorne's lean-time maker choice does not.

The competing-goods cards (x_honest_or_kind, x_loyalty_truth, x_dream_or_duty) produce genuinely uncomfortable, non-obvious beats. When they land on a life that has already accumulated relationships and a calling — like Noor Okonkwo's loyalty-vs-honesty choice at 59, coming after she'd married, had a child, and chosen the drifting life — they feel like pressure on a real character rather than a random moral test. The 'both are a kind of virtue' framing correctly refuses a clean answer.

The trait-affinity weighting in drawCard() (bookish child leans toward c_book, warm child toward c_friend, restless toward c_steal/c_move) produces a real divergence in early years that the transcripts confirm. Beatrix Okonkwo's 'guarded' trait routes her through c_talent -> 'Hide it', c_origin -> 'Take the world as it comes', and t_guarded in adulthood, creating a through-line. Cassian Thorne's 'frail' trait explicitly shapes his body-negotiation arc in ways that read as character-driven, not random.

Motto crystallization as a legible dynasty-layer payoff genuinely works at the session level. Seeing 'The family's character has settled, at last, into words: "We do not save ourselves for later"' (House Thorne) land in Cassian Thorne's life after Tomas chose the scholar road and nursed the sick creates a real feeling of earned identity — even if the motto itself is somewhat predictable once the reckless/generous flags are set.
staleness: The structural template for a 'settled' life is extremely consistent and visible across dynasties: c_origin -> (c_book or c_talent) -> y_calling -> y_love1 -> a_marry -> a_child -> a_fork_career or a_work -> m_health -> e_bequest -> epitaph. Seven of the 15 dynasties' founders walk within one or two beats of this sequence. The transcripts make this legible: Saoirse Holloway (D1), Cassian Achterberg (D3), Selma Quint (D9), Tobias Aldecott (D10), Ren Holloway (D11) all share the same broad shape. The variance within the template is high quality, but the template itself is always visible.

The body-decline observation pool is deep (18+ lines in the vit_tire bucket, 16+ in vit_neg) but fires in nearly every long life, always in the same phase (post-45), and the lines all share the same elegiac register and grammatical structure ('The stairs have started to ask a question', 'The body has begun sending its small bills', 'The weather has begun living in his joints'). Across 15 dynasties these accumulate into a predictable late-life texture. Dynasty 4's Beatrix, Dynasty 13's Anders, Dynasty 10's Felix, Dynasty 15's Ronja — all experience the same sequence of body-observation lines in the same tonal register, regardless of how different their vocational lives were.

The marriage beat (a_marry) fires in approximately 75% of lives that opened a love relationship, and most of the resulting 'Married X' lines share a family of templates ('The day was small and the meaning was not', 'Nobody made a speech; the years that followed were the speech', 'on an ordinary day, and meant every word of it'). Across the 15 dynasties this beat appears at least 20 times. The engine has deepened the pool (late-marriage variants, era-coloured framings) but the beat itself is structurally inescapable and the lines, while individually fine, blur together after the fifth or sixth instance.

The 'first child' narration (haveChild) uses a pool of 8 base lines plus 7 late-birth lines, but across multi-generation dynasties the lines visibly recur. In Dynasty 4 alone: Calla 'discovered a fear she had not known she owned', Elias 'Some door he hadn't known was shut came quietly open', Noor 'began, that night, keeping a different kind of time', Beatrix 'discovered a fear she had not known she owned' (identical to Calla's). The grandparent-birth callback (e_window) and the great-grandparent version generate the same texture two generations apart. The pool is large enough not to repeat verbatim often, but the register and beat are identical every time.

The 'drifter' arc resolves into a predictable reckoning structure that plays identically across multiple lives: y_adrift -> a_adrift (ache quietly for an anchor or lean into the range) -> m_adrift (grasp late for a single thing or make peace the drift was the life) -> elder epitaph about 'a way of being loose in the world'. Calla Okonkwo, Noor Okonkwo, Vesna Thorne, Mira Halloran, and Anders Aldecott all walk substantially the same philosophical arc, and the closing lines ('the drift was the life', 'wider than most if harder to name', 'was elsewhere as often as here') form a small, well-worn cluster. The drifter is structurally the same person every time.

The 'founding from nothing' beat (s_from_nothing) fires reliably for low-seat lives and produces near-identical outcomes: either 'Began from nothing, and laid the first course of something, alone' or 'Threw their lot in with others, and rose, slowly, alongside them'. These two lines appear in Dynasty 1 (Saoirse), Dynasty 3 (Cassian), Dynasty 5 (Ottilie), Dynasty 6 (Tomas), Dynasty 7 (Caleb), Dynasty 11 (Ren), Dynasty 12 (Mira), Dynasty 13 (Emory), Dynasty 14 (Greta), Dynasty 15 (Saoirse Brandt) — essentially every founder of a low-standing house. The lines themselves are good, but their near-universal appearance makes the founding moment feel procedural rather than particular.

improvements.what: Give the drifter arc 2-3 more structurally distinct resolutions. Currently all drifter lives collapse into the same philosophical reckoning ('was the drift the life, or was it waste?'). A drifter who had a child and a spouse could resolve into 'anchored by accident'; one with high-heart could become 'the connector, the one everyone converged on'; a low-spirit one could end in genuine regret rather than the gentle wistfulness that currently dominates. The resolution should depend on what else the life built, not just on the y_adrift choice.
improvements.why: Five drifter lives in 15 dynasties walked nearly identical philosophical arcs. Emergence for this lens means the drift should mean different things depending on the other systemic variables — but currently the drifter arc is structurally isolated from the rest of the life's accumulated flags.

improvements.what: Add vocation-specific death-phase observation lines to break the universal body-decline pool. Soldiers might have war-memory intrusions at night (the war card already exists — 'the war comes back at three in the morning' appears, but only as a callback, not as ambient texture). Scholars might get 'the mind is still the room the body doesn't lock'. Makers might notice what the hands can no longer do. Currently the body-decline observations are drawn from a single pool regardless of vocation, making late-life feel identical for a soldier and a scholar.
improvements.why: The body-decline pool is the loudest source of cross-dynasty staleness in the transcripts. Splitting it by vocation would make elder lives read more differently from each other without requiring new cards — just additional pools in observe().

improvements.what: Add a founding-from-something variant for dynasties that start above seat 1. Currently s_from_nothing fires for low-seat founders only, and high-seat founders get no equivalent structural beat — they just inherit the standing without a moment that dramatises what that means. A card gated on seat >= 3 at founding that presents 'you were born into a name that already means something, and the question is what you owe it' would make the high-seat founder feel distinct from the low-seat founder in the adult band.
improvements.why: Multi-generation dynasties that climb to seat 3-4 and then start a new collateral heir show this gap: the new heir begins with 'Born into a small house in town' but then proceeds through exactly the same adult arc as a founder who started in a rented room. The dynasty layer's accumulated standing doesn't shape the life enough.

improvements.what: Thin the 'founding moment' observations (s_from_nothing) in lives that are clearly not founders — heirs who are born into seat >= 2 should not see 'There is nothing behind them' because there is something behind them: the house. The card's cond checks seat <= 1 but in multi-gen dynasties the seat can drop after a bad generation, causing a 3rd-generation heir to be told they're starting from nothing when the player knows they have a motto and heirlooms.
improvements.why: This breaks the dynasty layer's narrative logic. When Hale Okonkwo (5th gen, 'old and famous house') sees 'Began from nothing, and laid the first course of something, alone', it actively undermines the dynasty's accumulated standing. The card's cond should cross-check gen as well as seat.

improvements.what: Introduce at least 2 callback cards that fire on a dynasty-level memory rather than a per-life memory — moments where THIS heir explicitly responds to an ancestor several generations back. The 'honour the first of the line' card (fired by Hale Okonkwo in Dynasty 4 and Anders Lindqvist in Dynasty 13) shows this is possible and it is the single most emotionally potent emergent beat in the transcripts. Expanding this to dynasty-level memories of the founding calling, the family's worst failure, or the first heirloom would give the dynasty layer a much stronger forward-pull than it currently has.
improvements.why: The cross-generational callback is the unique proposition of this genre — the thing action games cannot do. Currently it is underused: most callbacks are per-life (cb_books_late, cb_lookaway, cb_strayed) and only 'honour the first of the line' and the inherited-secret card reach back dynastically. Expanding this is the highest-leverage improvement available.

verdict: A Life is a genuine and sometimes excellent meditative life-sim with real systemic depth in its callback arcs, trait-affinity routing, and dynasty-layer mechanics — the five-generation Okonkwo dynasty in particular shows what the engine can do when everything compounds. The score is held to 6.4 rather than higher because the template is too visible: a player running three sessions in a row will recognize the founding-from-nothing beat, the universal body-decline texture, the drifter's philosophical reckoning, and the marriage/first-child sequence appearing at predictable intervals regardless of what else the life is doing. The variance is high quality but the scaffold shows through it. The most urgent fix is systemic: the drifter arc and the elder body arc both need to read differently depending on what the rest of the life built, which requires tying their resolution cards to accumulated flags rather than drawing from universal pools.
